candidates.evidence_text: How Hollyoaks saved the life of Manchester mental health activist - BBC News Image source, John Junior Image caption, "I felt like I couldn't tell anyone how I felt," John said. "I want others to hear my story and to know help is out there." By Georgie Docker North West Published 1 hour ago A mental health campaigner said they were seconds away from taking their own life before being saved by a plotline in a soap opera. John Junior, 37, from Wythenshawe, in Greater Manchester, had been suffering with depression since the age of 14. But after the sudden death of their father in 2018, the then-IT worker said they hit rock bottom. During lockdown in 2020, John was contemplating taking their own life when a Hollyoaks storyline stopped them in their tracks. "I seconds away from ending my life," John recalled. "I had Hollyoaks on in the background and I turned round to watch the scene. "There was a moment when a character was told her partner had taken his own life. "Something happened to me and it gave me enough time to think beyond what I was about to do. "I wouldn't be here today if it wasn't for Hollyoaks." Ahead of World Suicide Prevention Day 2026, on 10 September, John said now they want to share their experience to encourage others to speak out. Warning: This article contains references to and details of self-harm, suicide, and suicidal ideations. The BBC Action Line has details of a range of advice and support for anyone affected by the issues raised Image source, John Junior Image caption, John Junior, 37, from Wythenshawe, said an episode of Hollyoaks had stopped them from taking their own life John said they had suffered with their mental health for more than a decade before hitting rock bottom after the death of their father in March 2018. "I was diagnosed with depression when I was 14," they said. "It had been a part of my life but I was wearing a mask constantly. "My father's death pushed me over the edge - it was a shock." Three days afterwards, John said they attempted to take their own life for the first time. "I didn't want to die, I wanted that feeling, that pain to stop," they said. 'Feeling small' After being discharged from hospital, John sought help from their GP and from psychiatric services. And in 2019 they were diagnosed as having Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) - a personality disorder which affects mood and interactions with others , external . "When I had the diagnosis I thought it was brilliant," John recalled. "I had been unaware my symptoms of depression were indicative of BPD. "I thought I was going to get the help that I needed." But John, who currently lives in Wilmslow, in Cheshire, said they were told the treatment required, known as Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), was not available in the area. DBT is a recognised NHS treatment for BPD , external . It is a form of psychotherapy with a focus on self acceptance - according to mental health charity Mind , external , DBT is "specially adapted for people who feel emotions very intensely". John said they felt lost without access to this NHS treatment. "It made me feel horrible and like I was small," they said. "You've just been given a diagnosis of the most complex mental health disorders and I didn't have the right support." Image source, John Junior Image caption, John became a mental health advocate and campaigner from 2020 But in 2020, John decided to make a second attempt on their own life. "I was literally on my computer and I had Hollyoaks on in the background just playing away," John said. "I had started watching it again during lockdown. "And I heard a knock at a door in the episode. "I started watching it and it was two police officers telling a character, Nancy Hayton, played by Jessica Fox, that her boyfriend Kyle Kelly, played by Adam Rickett, had taken his own life. "Something inside me changed as I realised that could be my mum or my brother. "I had been planning to take my life in that moment and it was like I was being shackled down and I couldn't move. "To this day I can't put it into words - it literally just released me from these shackles, released me from these chains, and I felt free." Image source, Channel 4/Lime Pictures Image caption, Hollyoaks character Nancy found out her boyfriend had taken his own life on 9 June 2020 Since then John launched a campaign with their local MP Esther McVey to help others access DBT. candidates.lead: More than 30 stores have been closed over their links to the sale of illegal vapes and cigarettes
candidates.evidence_text: Inside the crackdown on illegal vapes in north-west England - BBC News Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, Retail researchers estimate that there are about 3,600 specialist vape shops in the UK By Rachel Braund North West Published 6 September 2026 Police forces and councils across north-west England have shut vape shops and seized thousands of illegal items in the last year, new figures show. BBC analysis found more than 30 premises have been closed over their links to illegal vapes and illicit tobacco. The findings come after the Prime Minister announced plans to give councils greater powers to tackle rogue retailers and extend closure orders. Authorities say the products can pose a risk to public health and are often linked to wider criminality. Greater Manchester In Greater Manchester, police and council officers seized thousands of illegal vapes and cigarettes as part of Operation Elswick, a joint campaign targeting rogue retailers. In Manchester alone, officers removed £162,000 worth of illegal vapes from sale in the last year. Det Ch Insp Chris Woodburn, from Greater Manchester Police, said: "Our work in this area will continue as we are committed to tackling the issue of illegal vapes and cigarettes which fund wider crime and harm public health." Elsewhere, Bury Council obtained its first closure order against a shop after more than 3,000 vaping products were seized, while Rochdale recorded nine vape shop closures in the last six months. Image caption, Specialist dogs were part of the team searching premises in Operation Elswick Merseyside Liverpool City Council said it had secured 10 closure orders in the past six months, although it stressed these were linked to corner shops selling illicit tobacco rather than vaping products alone. In Wirral, Liscard Convenience Store became the 20th premises to be closed down since December 2025 after a closure order was granted by magistrates. Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, Lancashire Police worked with officers at the council to close down two shops in Lancaster Lancashire In Lancashire, six vape shops have been closed and a further seven are currently being investigated. Lancashire Police and Trading Standards recently secured closure orders against two Lancaster city centre retailers after a series of failed inspections and test purchases. Euro Shop was found to have sold vapes to underage test purchasers as well as illicit cigarettes, while One Stop Mini Market repeatedly failed Trading Standards checks. Both were ordered to close until November. Sending a 'clear message' Supt Abbott, from Lancashire Police, said: "Securing a closure order is not a quick process. "It often takes months of dedicated work by our officers and partners to gather evidence, build a strong case and present it before the courts. "This result reflects the determination and professionalism of everyone involved in bringing these matters to a successful conclusion. "We take the concerns of our communities seriously and listen to the information provided by residents, businesses and local partners. "That information plays a vital role in helping us identify issues, gather evidence and take positive action where it is needed." Image source, PA Media Image caption, The ONS estimates that 5.4 million people aged 16+ in the UK used e-cigarettes daily Cheshire Cheshire Police has secured closure orders against 12 shops linked to illegal vape sales, including premises in Warrington, Widnes, Macclesfield, Crewe and Nantwich. Ch Supt Saf Ali said the action should send "a clear message" that illegal tobacco and vape products have no place in the county's shops. How is the government tackling it? The crackdown on vape shops announced by the government in August includes the following proposals: Changes to planning law in England which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes or vapes would need to apply to their local council for permission to open Tightening the definition of a vape shop in England to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres in England, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops in England and Wales found to be selling illegal tobacco for up to 12 months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer Related topics Cheshire More on this s

candidates.lead: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
candidates.evidence_text: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations - BBC News Image caption, The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is on display at Wardley Hall By Jen Dale North West Published 6 September 2026 On 25 April 1641, Ambrose Barlow celebrated a secret Easter Sunday mass at Morleys Hall near Astley in Greater Manchester. But, by the end of the service, the building had been surrounded by a 400-strong armed group led by a local vicar. "King Charles I issued a decree stating that all Catholic priests must leave within a month...and if they didn't, they would face the consequences of treason," said the Right Reverend John Arnold, the Bishop of Salford. King Charles I wanted to prove that he supported the Protestant faith while keeping his political enemies at bay as parliament were suspicious of his Catholic wife. The congregation urged Ambrose Barlow to hide but Arnold said he refused and instead ordered the doors to be opened and surrendered peacefully. "He didn't make any attempt to avoid arrest," said Arnold. "He was really concerned for the safety of the people attending mass - about 150 of them." Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, The Right Reverend John Arnold said records showed Ambrose Barlow had a "good sense of humour" and was "very mild in his character" He was taken to Lancaster Castle where he was imprisoned. After four months, he was put on trial, charged with being a priest. He was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death. "On 10 September, which is now his feast day, he was hung, drawn, and quartered," said Arnold. "And his skull was put on a pike as a demonstration to people that this is what happens if you are a Catholic." It was a warning to all who refused to conform to the state religion. Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, Wardley Hall has been the residence of the Bishop of Salford since 1930 The Catholic priest is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds. The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is a sacred relic, which is kept at Wardley Hall in Worsley on red velvet inside a locked, glass-fronted cabinet recessed into a wall on the main staircase. Arnold said the skull was retrieved and brought to Wardley Hall, which has been the residence of the Bishop of Salford since 1930. "At that stage Wardley Hall belonged to the Downes family who were the cousins to the Barlow family," said Arnold, who resides at Wardley Hall. "Francis Downes placed the skull in a casket in the wall of the then chapel in Wardley Hall." The skull was accidentally discovered by Matthew Moreton during renovation work in 1745. The Skull of a Saint at Wardley Hall In 1641, Catholic priest Ambrose Barlow was persecuted for his beliefs. Listen on Sounds Later forensic tests in the 20th century confirmed it was the skull of Ambrose Barlow. On 25 October 1970, Pope Paul VI officially canonised 40 martyrs of England and Wales in a ceremony at St Peter's Basilica in Rome. This honoured Catholic men and women killed in the 16th and 17th centuries for their beliefs. Ambrose Barlow became Saint Ambrose Barlow. The skull of St Ambrose Barlow remains at Wardley Hall where private groups can see it by appointment. Arnold said it was unusual to have such a relic in a private collection. "It's rare for it to be in a private house, but Catholics have long had a tradition of relics, either pieces of a body of a saint or a possession of a saint," he said. "It's a way people have found of coming closer to the reality of the holiness of the person." You can listen to the Hidden Manchester series on BBC Sounds. Often the last day of school was the last time you saw most class mates - even if you might not realise it at the time It was something that prompted grandmother Karen Feay to track down the people she started Rivington & Blackrod Grammar School in Bolton with 60 years ago "I bumped into an old school friend and we got talking about our school memories - and it snowballed from there," she said. "We all started in 1966 which makes everyone 70 or 71 years old now." Karen and her friend Susan Hart have spent the past two years tracking down fellow school mates on social media A task she said had been more difficult for women who had changed their surnames after getting married

In March, this year, she got a call back to receive her results and when she heard it was breast cancer, she was left feeling as though her world was falling apart "I'm not someone who really worries so I was convinced in my head that it wasn't cancer," recalls Natalie. candidates.lead: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves?
candidates.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. James Anderton had the support of Margaret Thatcher and used his position to ord View 7 Images Sir James Anderton was Greater Manchester Police's chief constable at the time

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 16:39, 06 Sep 2026 View New Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges has revealed his ‘top priority’ for the city - and shared his plans to address issues such as rising rent prices which are making life difficult for thousands of Mancunians In his first interview since being appointed council leader on Thursday night, Councillor Bridges told the Manchester Evening News (MEN) how he wants to see Manchester change, spoke about his plans for Strangeways prison, and admitted which football team he supports He responded to the possibility of him losing his seat in the Old Moat ward next year after the Green Party won the area in this May’s local elections, and said that Manchester needs to ‘push developers to have more affordable housing in all and every development' in the city The new leader was voted by Labour councillors this week as the successor to Bev Craig who was elected as Greater Manchester mayor in July Asked what his message would be for the corners of Manchester which feel left behind from the city's success, Garry Bridges said: “The message from me is that those places that have felt left behind are my top priority, that is literally what we're here to do

candidates.evidence_text: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:22, 06 Sep 2026 Two years ago Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, together with his brother and mother who was sporting a black eye, appeared at a press conference in a fancy suite at Manchester's Midland Hotel They didn't speak a word but they looked suitably solemn as their lawyer held them up to be a virtuous pro-police family - some of them serving police officers - who had been the victim of shocking and unprovoked police brutality at Manchester Airport six days earlier Not only that but they were then subjected to a 'deliberate attempt to smear them' by someone inside GMP That was because, two days before the press conference, the Manchester Evening News obtained and then published CCTV footage which provided some context to the by then infamous violence which erupted in the pay station at Terminal 2 at the airport It was a clip that gave perspective to earlier mobile phone footage of an armed police officer kicking the face of Amaaz as he lay prone and motionless on the ground

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble... but he was not choosing his friends wisely" View 7 Images Julius Matera was 43 when he died News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:08, 06 Sep 2026 Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was pronounced dead by paramedics at ten minutes past noon on December 8, 2023. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. He suffered catastrophic blood loss on the night of October 13 and 14 that year Known as Julius, he had been reported missing on October 24, but by then he had already been dead a week. It was 56 days later and in dramatic fashion that his body was found But an explosive inquest at Bolton coroners court heard how a wall of silence has meant his family have been denied justice in what they believe is a case of murder View 7 Images Julius was described as "quite literally a gentle man"

candidates.evidence_text: Blackpool Mum's fight for son's medical records after tragic E.coli death following Blackpool beach swim Rachael Bell believes her son Matthew's death in 1997 may have been linked to sewage at a beach near Blackpool, and spent nearly three decades try A Lancashire mother who suspects her young son's death almost 30 years ago may have been connected to sewage contamination at a beach near Blackpool has opened up about her battle to access his medical records Rachael Bell, 61, revealed she spent decades carrying the burden of guilt over the death of her beloved son Matthew, who passed away aged just under four in 1997. Matthew initially experienced diarrhoea and severe stomach cramps before his condition became critical He was diagnosed with E. coli O157, amongst the most hazardous strains of the bacteria, and subsequently developed haemolytic uraemic syndrome, a rare complication that can result in kidney failure Matthew's younger brother Tom also fell ill with the same infection but fortunately made a full recovery Matthew's health worsened and he was transferred to Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool . Following several harrowing weeks, he slipped into a coma and was relocated to intensive care before his tragic death towards the end of October, reports Lancs Live

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport 'She was like a sister, but it was cancer which brought us closer together again' Natalie Luxton said her breast cancer diagnosis brought her 'closer together' with a childhood neighbour and friend News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 17:36, 06 Natalie Luxton had been preparing to celebrate her husband's birthday with a trip to Centre Parcs when she noticed a lump on her right side. She assumed it would be nothing but as she had the day off work decided to get it checked The 39-year-old, from Stockport , had a biopsy but left assuming she would get the all-clear. In March, this year, she got a call back to receive her results and when she heard it was breast cancer, she was left feeling as though her world was falling apart "I'm not someone who really worries so I was convinced in my head that it wasn't cancer," recalls Natalie. "I've heard mixed stories where people have gone back in and had the results and it wasn't. So the fact we did have to go back didn't worry me too much "We sat down and the consultant said talk me through what you know up to now. So I started talking through the process up to that point and he just said, 'okay, I'm sorry to tell you you've got breast cancer' View 6 Images Natalie Luxton with her husband (Image: Supplied)

candidates.lead: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves?
candidates.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. James Anderton had the support of Margaret Thatcher and used his position to ord View 7 Images Sir James Anderton was Greater Manchester Police's chief constable at the time

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Council Meet Manchester council's new leader - what he's got planned for the city Garry Bridges was elected as the new leader of Manchester City Council this week. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 16:39, 06 Sep 2026 View New Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges has revealed his ‘top priority’ for the city - and shared his plans to address issues such as rising rent prices which are making life difficult for thousands of Mancunians In his first interview since being appointed council leader on Thursday night, Councillor Bridges told the Manchester Evening News (MEN) how he wants to see Manchester change, spoke about his plans for Strangeways prison, and admitted which football team he supports He responded to the possibility of him losing his seat in the Old Moat ward next year after the Green Party won the area in this May’s local elections, and said that Manchester needs to ‘push developers to have more affordable housing in all and every development' in the city The new leader was voted by Labour councillors this week as the successor to Bev Craig who was elected as Greater Manchester mayor in July Asked what his message would be for the corners of Manchester which feel left behind from the city's success, Garry Bridges said: “The message from me is that those places that have felt left behind are my top priority, that is literally what we're here to do

candidates.lead: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime r
candidates.evidence_text: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:22, 06 Sep 2026 Two years ago Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, together with his brother and mother who was sporting a black eye, appeared at a press conference in a fancy suite at Manchester's Midland Hotel They didn't speak a word but they looked suitably solemn as their lawyer held them up to be a virtuous pro-police family - some of them serving police officers - who had been the victim of shocking and unprovoked police brutality at Manchester Airport six days earlier Not only that but they were then subjected to a 'deliberate attempt to smear them' by someone inside GMP That was because, two days before the press conference, the Manchester Evening News obtained and then published CCTV footage which provided some context to the by then infamous violence which erupted in the pay station at Terminal 2 at the airport It was a clip that gave perspective to earlier mobile phone footage of an armed police officer kicking the face of Amaaz as he lay prone and motionless on the ground

candidates.summary: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble

candidates.lead: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
candidates.evidence_text: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble... but he was not choosing his friends wisely" View 7 Images Julius Matera was 43 when he died News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:08, 06 Sep 2026 Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was pronounced dead by paramedics at ten minutes past noon on December 8, 2023. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. He suffered catastrophic blood loss on the night of October 13 and 14 that year Known as Julius, he had been reported missing on October 24, but by then he had already been dead a week. It was 56 days later and in dramatic fashion that his body was found But an explosive inquest at Bolton coroners court heard how a wall of silence has meant his family have been denied justice in what they believe is a case of murder View 7 Images Julius was described as "quite literally a gentle man"

But locals say there is something missing The Rochdale borough town has no trams running through, no train stations and a bus service that takes around an hour to get to Manchester city centre . The journey time between Heywood and Manchester is around 30 minutes by car So last year, when Andy Burnham announced there would be spades in the ground on the new tram link for Heywood by 2028, there was elation Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project which falls under what TfGM’s Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder scheme The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved

candidates.evidence_text: Blackpool Mum's fight for son's medical records after tragic E.coli death following Blackpool beach swim Rachael Bell believes her son Matthew's death in 1997 may have been linked to sewage at a beach near Blackpool, and spent nearly three decades try A Lancashire mother who suspects her young son's death almost 30 years ago may have been connected to sewage contamination at a beach near Blackpool has opened up about her battle to access his medical records Rachael Bell, 61, revealed she spent decades carrying the burden of guilt over the death of her beloved son Matthew, who passed away aged just under four in 1997. Matthew initially experienced diarrhoea and severe stomach cramps before his condition became critical He was diagnosed with E. coli O157, amongst the most hazardous strains of the bacteria, and subsequently developed haemolytic uraemic syndrome, a rare complication that can result in kidney failure Matthew's younger brother Tom also fell ill with the same infection but fortunately made a full recovery Matthew's health worsened and he was transferred to Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool . Following several harrowing weeks, he slipped into a coma and was relocated to intensive care before his tragic death towards the end of October, reports Lancs Live

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City FC Coventry FC fans entered Droylsden shop, 'stole £250 worth of booze, assaulted staff and left' after Man City defeat 'These are fathers and grandfathers laughing and putting things in their pockets as if they're teenage kids' Commen A Droylsden shop owner has spoken out after a group of Coventry City fans shoplifted and allegedly assaulted a member of his staff on Saturday (September 6) The owner of Go Local Manor Convenience said that, following their loss against Manchester City at the Etihad, around 15 away fans came into his shop and walked out with over £250 worth of alcohol and other items The fans, who were travelling by coach and 'probably intoxicated from the game', then assaulted the member of staff working at the shop when he tried to stop them from leaving The owner said: "They were coming off the coach and just giving all sorts of abuse to the staff member and one of them at first tried walking out with a load of alcohol View 2 Images CCTV footage from the shop shows the fans inside during the incident (Image: Go Local Manor Convenience)

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Stockport mum was drug driving when her partner fell out of van and died Stockport mum Emma Foden has been sentenced after David Rhodes' death Comments News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 09:10, 06 Sep 2026 Upda A Stockport mum was behind the wheel of a van while over the limit for cannabis when her partner fell from the back and died from his injuries - in front of their seven-year-old daughter Emma Foden, 46, had been driving the Peugeot Bippa along Dowbridge in Kirkham, near Blackpool , when David Rhodes fell from the back and banged his head on the road. He was rushed to Royal Preston Hospital with severe head injuries, a court heard But he died later on October 11 last year, Lancs Live reports . Foden has now been sentenced for drug driving in Preston Magistrates' Court In an emotional statement read in court, Rhodes' loved ones said: "There isn't a day we don't think about him." The court heard an investigation had found Foden was not responsible for the accident A conclusion of misadventure was recorded following an earlier inquest at Blackpool Coroners' Court. But following the collision, Foden was tested for alcohol and drugs and was found to be over the legal limit for cannabis

candidates.lead: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves?
candidates.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. James Anderton had the support of Margaret Thatcher and used his position to ord View 7 Images Sir James Anderton was Greater Manchester Police's chief constable at the time

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 16:39, 06 Sep 2026 View New Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges has revealed his ‘top priority’ for the city - and shared his plans to address issues such as rising rent prices which are making life difficult for thousands of Mancunians In his first interview since being appointed council leader on Thursday night, Councillor Bridges told the Manchester Evening News (MEN) how he wants to see Manchester change, spoke about his plans for Strangeways prison, and admitted which football team he supports He responded to the possibility of him losing his seat in the Old Moat ward next year after the Green Party won the area in this May’s local elections, and said that Manchester needs to ‘push developers to have more affordable housing in all and every development' in the city The new leader was voted by Labour councillors this week as the successor to Bev Craig who was elected as Greater Manchester mayor in July Asked what his message would be for the corners of Manchester which feel left behind from the city's success, Garry Bridges said: “The message from me is that those places that have felt left behind are my top priority, that is literally what we're here to do

candidates.evidence_text: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:22, 06 Sep 2026 Two years ago Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, together with his brother and mother who was sporting a black eye, appeared at a press conference in a fancy suite at Manchester's Midland Hotel They didn't speak a word but they looked suitably solemn as their lawyer held them up to be a virtuous pro-police family - some of them serving police officers - who had been the victim of shocking and unprovoked police brutality at Manchester Airport six days earlier Not only that but they were then subjected to a 'deliberate attempt to smear them' by someone inside GMP That was because, two days before the press conference, the Manchester Evening News obtained and then published CCTV footage which provided some context to the by then infamous violence which erupted in the pay station at Terminal 2 at the airport It was a clip that gave perspective to earlier mobile phone footage of an armed police officer kicking the face of Amaaz as he lay prone and motionless on the ground

candidates.lead: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
candidates.evidence_text: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble... but he was not choosing his friends wisely" View 7 Images Julius Matera was 43 when he died News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:08, 06 Sep 2026 Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was pronounced dead by paramedics at ten minutes past noon on December 8, 2023. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. He suffered catastrophic blood loss on the night of October 13 and 14 that year Known as Julius, he had been reported missing on October 24, but by then he had already been dead a week. It was 56 days later and in dramatic fashion that his body was found But an explosive inquest at Bolton coroners court heard how a wall of silence has meant his family have been denied justice in what they believe is a case of murder View 7 Images Julius was described as "quite literally a gentle man"

It was part of a wider drive to 'ensure the country never again faces the nightmare of running out of prison spaces' But well-placed sources here in Manchester hope the move could help town hall bosses bolster their case for the potential closure of Strangeways. It comes three months after the MEN revealed that 'promising conversations' had been taking place with government about relocating the Speaking this week, Cheetham councillor Naeem Hassan welcomed the announcement of the new prison and said he hopes it helps usher in the end of Strangeways He said: "It's such a prime location in the city. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham 'Explosions' heard in Oldham as firefighters scrambled and over 100 homes without power Locals have reported hearing loud bangs before emergency services attended the scene Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:44, 05 Sep 2026 View Imag More than 100 homes were left without power after a fire at an electrical substation in Oldham. Locals reported hearing 'loud bangs' and 'explosions' as the fire broke out at the substation on Harewood Drive in Royton A video posted to social media showed bright orange flames lapping up inside it and smoke billowing out. The fire service were alerted with two fire engines attending the scene at around 5:10pm this evening (Saturday, September 5). Police were also said to be in attendance Firefighters used dry powder extinguishers in order to put out the blaze. No one was injured, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said Scores of locals on the neighbouring Thorp estate say their power cut out following the fire, with lights going out and dozens of house alarms sounding in the area simultaneously According to Electricity North West (ENW), at the time of writing, a total of 147 properties were still without power

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.evidence_text: Paul Sharpe, 56, bundled his teenage victim into a car in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, on 18 May Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Sharpe - jailed in 2001 for murdering an ex-partner - had been to the area months before and had recorded voice memos detailing his planned "abduction point" Sharpe, from Portswood, Stockport, was ordered to serve a minimum of eight years in jail before he can be considered for release by the Parole Board The court heard the teenager was kept captive in Sharpe's car for eight and a half hours before she was rescued by police the following day In fear that she was going to be raped and murdered, she showed "an astonishing presence of mind" to tear out strands of hair to provide DNA proof she had been in the vehicle, the court was told Sharpe, who strangled his former partner in 2000, had been released on licence from prison in 2013, for which he had been given a life sentence with a minimum term of 11 years

candidates.source_evidence: Cllr Garry Bridges is set to be appointed as the new Leader of Manchester City Council at a special meeting this week (Thursday 3 September, 6pm) Cllr Bridges succeeds Cllr Bev Craig, who was elected as Greater Manchester Mayor in July, having previously served as statutory Deputy Leader since 2024. Subject to confirmation at the full Council meeting, he will take up the political leadership of the Council The Leader has ultimate responsibility for setting the long-term vision for the Council at the heart of Manchester’s ongoing inclusive growth, leading a team of Executive (Cabinet) members. He will represent the Council – and the city – at regional, national and international lev Cllr Bridges’ political priority has been ensuring that Manchester’s young people have the best start in life and have the opportunities, through work and skills, to share in the city’s success Prior to becoming Deputy Leader in 2024, Cllr Bridges had held the position of Executive Member for Children and Schools and overseen significant improvements across children’s services – which are now rated Outstanding by Ofsted. This included championing free school meals durin His commitment has been accentuated by his role as a parent to two toddlers, a daughter (aged three) and a son (aged four.)

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

candidates.evidence_text: A shop in Leigh town centre has been closed for three months following repeated seizures of illicit tobacco products Wigan Council’s Trading Standards team, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police, secured the closure order for Shop & Save on Bradshawgate after concerns were raised about illegal sales Following an investigation by Trading Standards, a three-month closure order was approved at Wigan and Leigh Magistrates Court on Thursday, 3rd September Councillor Kevin Anderson, portfolio holder for police, crime and civil contingencies said: "This closure order yet again demonstrates our commitment to tackling illegal trading and protecting our communities across Wigan Borough “Traders who engage in this kind of activity will not be allowed to continue breaking the law, and we will continue working with partners to investigate reports of illicit sales and take robust action where unlawful activity is identified.” Over the course of two months, Trading Standards officers seized 7,380 sticks of illicit cigarettes and four kilograms of illicit hand rolling tobacco, which was concealed in elaborate hides within the premises

candidates.evidence_text: Businesses, makers and event organisers are being invited to register their interest in Wigan's new market hall ahead of its opening next year Wigan Market at Fettlers, operated by Wigan Council, will open in the spring as the centrepiece of the wider Fettlers development, bringing the market back to the heart of Wigan town centre The council would like to build a picture of businesses that would like to be part of the new venue, alongside existing market traders The new facility will have space for a wider mix of independent retail, fresh food, street food and kitchens, bars and cafes, makers, services, and a programme of events and entertainment throughout the day and into the evening Councillor Dane Anderton, portfolio holder for economic development and regeneration, said: "Wigan has been a market town for centuries, and this is a real moment for the town “Our current traders are at the heart of the new market and we're working closely with them on the move, and now we want to hear from the businesses, makers and performers who would like to join them and help shape something Wigan can be proud of

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. candidates.evidence_text: GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones Hosted by Joe McGrath. To register your interest email greg@grubmcr.com

candidates.evidence_text: ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Павел Дедищев выступит в Лондоне со своим стендап концертом "АМЕРИКАНЕЦ" Лондон! 30го сентября к нам приезжает Павел Дедищев со своим концертом "Американец" Резидент шоу Stand Up на ТНТ, финалист «Comedy Баттл» и «Большого шоу», участник проектов «Решалы» и «Было слово». Он стоял у истоков объединения HIT2SHIT (будущего Labelcom), стал сооснователем канала «Комьюнити» и одним из тех, кто формировал новую волну русскоязычного стендапа. Павел Дедищев - комик с ярко выраженным собственным стилем, в котором сочетаются честность, дерзость и умение подмечать детали, знакомые каждому. Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. Дедищев говорит прямо, не сглаживает углы и именно этим вызывает у зрителей тот самый взрывной смех. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:45 End: 21:30 Мы работаем по принципу first come, first served, а именно, кто пришел раньше, то и занял лучшее место. 18+ P.S. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. Having cleared There could, and probably should have been more City goals and as well as Rayan Cherki being at the heart of the team's creativity again there were positive signs from the transfer window. Elliot Anderson purred along in midfield and Enzo Fernandez tuned straight into City wavele Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! candidates.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне В Лондоне прозвучит украинская песня, и снова найдет своих людей, ведь на сцену выйдет Наталка Карпа — певица, чей голос уже более двух десятилетий остается голосом света и искренней любви к родной земле. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона!
